title: Request Ledger: combined latency + cost timeline with rollout overlays
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Overview: Design a lightweight "Request Ledger" panel that surfaces a single-row timeline per request combining span/timing markers with a per-segment cost sparkline and an overlay showing model rollout/version boundaries. Purpose is to let engineers and SREs quickly answer: ‘how much did this request cost, where did latency occur, and which model versions served which tokens?’

Core components: 
- Single-line request timeline: visualizes request lifecycle (ingest, routing, model call(s), post-process) as proportional segments.
- Span markers: compact icons for errors, retries, cache hits, fallback triggers. Hover reveals span metadata (service, duration, trace id).
- Cost sparkline: miniature per-token or per-segment cost bar beneath timeline, with hover tooltip showing token range and estimated token-cost breakdown.
- Rollout overlays: translucent color bands on timeline indicating which model variant/version handled token ranges; clicking band shows rollout config and % traffic at time of request.
- Correlation ID band: copyable correlation/request id, and quick jump to full trace in Trace Inspector.
- Filters & quick actions: filter by cost threshold, latency bucket, model version, and toggle 'show only non-cache spans'.

Design constraints & trade-offs: 
- Must remain visually compact so list views can show many requests without vertical blowup.
- Cost attribution granularity depends on telemetry: ideal is per-token but fallback to per-model-call estimates if token-level telemetry is unavailable.
- UI must not trigger heavy server work; prefer precomputed per-request cost metadata surfaced via logs/observability pipeline.
- Rollout overlay accuracy depends on request-time routing logs; if missing, show 'approximate' badge.

Success criteria / metrics: 
- Engineers can triage cost spikes: time-to-identify root cause under 3 minutes in 80% of usability tests.
- Reduction in support tickets asking ‘why did this request cost X’ by 30% in first quarter post-release.

Accessibility: colorblind-safe palette for rollout overlays; rollovers have accessible labels; keyboard focus on timeline segments should reveal tooltip content in a side panel for screen readers.

Handoff artifacts: Figma prototype (link below), interaction spec, handoff token formats for backend telemetry team.
comments: 2026-02-12 - PM review (Jon Park): Strong signal for cost + latency in the list view. PM requests a tiny mode for dense lists (1-line per request) and an expanded mode that shows 3rd-party service timings.

2026-02-18 - Eng sync (Leah Ortiz): Backend needs to emit 'request_cost_breakdown' with token ranges or we provide cost estimates with a confidence flag. KV cache hit/span visibility feasible via current tracing header. Need sampling when volume is high.
2026-02-22 - Design critique (internal): Move rollout legend to hover; avoid persistent legend to save horizontal space. Replace percentage labels with microtooltips to keep timeline uncluttered.
2026-02-25 - Prototype update (Aisha): Added keyboard focus state and ARIA labels; adjusted color ramp for Deuteranopia. Updated Figma frame to include compact and expanded states.
2026-02-28 - Usability note (session 03): Users expect 'jump-to-logs' and 'open in trace inspector' on right-click; added contextual menu in prototype.
